title: Retention Sculptor and Evidence Assembly for Request Artifacts
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Background: Customers need a way to precisely define TTLs for interactive artifacts (prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics) that is easy to reason about, auditable, and produces a compact machine- and human-readable evidence bundle for audits. Current retention UIs and export tooling are fragmented: per-route TTLs exist, but there is no single flow to preview effective TTLs across inheritance rules, nor a reproducible evidence manifest used in compliance bundles.

Goal: Deliver a ‘Retention Sculptor’ UX and backend orchestrator that lets tenants author TTL rules (global -> project -> route -> session sampler), preview the resolved TTL for any request type, simulate the eviction timeline, and export a signed Evidence Assembly (manifest + sample exports) suitable for compliance reviews. The feature should support residency-aware retention (region pinning) and be auditable (hashes + signatures).

Scope (MVP):
- Schema for TTL rules covering prompts, responses, request-logs, and metrics with default inheritance semantics.
- Console UI: interactive rule authoring, effective-TTL preview, and simulation timeline control.
- Backend: deterministic TTL resolver service, dry-run simulator, and evidence manifest generator (JSONL manifest + provenance hashes).
- Export: one-click evidence bundle (manifest + sample exports + signed checksum) for legal/compliance teams.
- Integrations: KMS-signed manifest, audit-log entry for rule changes, and a lightweight retention-preview API for integrators.

Non-goals (MVP): automated cross-region archival, per-token cryptographic redaction, and full data-migration tooling.

Success metrics:
- 80% of compliance-related support tickets referencing retention are resolvable via the evidence bundle within 48 hours.
- 50% reduction in manual evidence-assembly time for audited tenants.
- No SLA regressions for request latency in hosted API (<= 2% P95 increase during simulations).

Constraints & tradeoffs:
- Evidence manifests must be compact for large tenants: we will support sampled exports with deterministic seed-based sampling to produce reproducible samples instead of exporting full datasets in MVP.
- Residency: enforcement of region-bound TTLs is an infra concern — MVP will attach residency metadata to manifest entries and flag mismatches, while enforcement will be a follow-up ENG epic.

Open questions:
- Should sampled evidence include anonymized PII or only raw prompts/responses for tenants under enterprise contracts? (Legal/Privacy ops input required.)
- Storage model for proof-of-assembly signatures: in manifest only, or also a signed key-value in audit logs?

Links & artifacts:
- PRD: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PRD-Compliance-Retention-Sculptor
- Design mockups (console flows): https://www.figma.com/file/Retention-Sculptor/Console-UX
- Spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/Retention-Sculptor-Spec
- Prototype retention-resolver API definition: https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-proto/pull/12
- Incident learnings (retention purge race): https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-retention-race

Notes for Eng: deterministic behavior is critical for evidence reproducibility: include PRNG seed in manifest, a clear tie between request_id -> exported sample entry, and store cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) of exported artifacts. For KMS signing, follow console-2025-kms-patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tenant can create and save TTL rules with inheritance precedence visible in the UI.
- The effective-TTL preview returns a deterministic timeline for a given route and sample request id.
- Evidence bundle generator creates a manifest.jsonl with per-entry: request_id, artifact_kind, residency_tag, ttl_seconds, sample_seed, sha256_hash, created_at.
- Manifest can be signed with tenant KMS key and verified by a tool included in the bundle.
- Audit log entry created for TTL rule changes with diff and actor attribution.

Out-of-scope items to track separately:
- Cross-region enforced deletion (ENG follow-up: ENG-32100).
- Per-token redaction + homomorphic proofs (research).

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal alpha: feature-flagged for internal tenants + SRE testing (2 weeks).
2) Controlled beta: 5 pilot tenants (security review + legal approvals).
3) Public GA: documented in Compliance Controls launch notes, SDKs updated.

Risk mitigation:
- To avoid mass accidental purges, any newly authored TTL that shortens retention by > 30% must require two-step confirmation and create a dry-run report.
- Sampling randomness must be reproducible; store seeds centrally and include in manifest.

Request for reviewers: Eng to validate manifest schema and signer flow. Security to confirm KMS integration pattern. Legal/Privacy to sign off on sampled export policy and PII handling. Design to finalize export UX and preview simulator visuals.
